sections.content: If you've been searching for affordable markets with real upside potential, real estate deals in Huntington WV deserve a serious look. Located in the heart of the tri-state area where West Virginia, Kentucky, and Ohio meet, Huntington offers some of the lowest entry prices in the country combined with a stable rental base anchored by Marshall University and a regional medical hub. Whether you're a seasoned wholesaler or just getting started — check out this guide on [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) — Huntington's market has something to offer at nearly every experience level.
Huntington WV Market Overview

Huntington is West Virginia's second-largest city with a population of around 45,000 residents. The local economy leans on healthcare, education, and logistics. Cabell Huntington Hospital and St. Mary's Medical Center are two of the region's largest employers, creating consistent demand for workforce housing. Marshall University adds another layer of rental demand, particularly for smaller units and student-adjacent properties. The city has faced economic headwinds over the years, including population decline and blight, but that same environment is exactly what creates opportunity for value-add investors.
Average Home Prices and What Your Dollar Buys

As of 2024, the median home price in Huntington hovers around $95,000 to $115,000, making it one of the most affordable mid-size cities in the eastern United States. Entry-level single-family homes in working-class neighborhoods can be found for $40,000 to $65,000, while fully renovated properties in desirable areas top out around $175,000 to $200,000. This price ceiling is important to understand before you commit capital — Huntington is not a high-appreciation market, but the cash-on-cash returns for buy-and-hold investors can be exceptional. A $70,000 property renting for $850 per month is not unusual, which translates to a gross rent multiplier well below 10.

Before you make an offer on any Huntington property, run the numbers using our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to estimate after-repair value based on local comps. Knowing your ceiling helps you avoid overpaying in a market with a hard price cap.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Huntington WV
Not every neighborhood in Huntington will work for every strategy. Here's a breakdown of the areas that investors consistently target and why.
Westmoreland and Enslow Park

These established residential neighborhoods on the west side of the city are the sweet spot for buy-and-hold landlords and flippers alike. Homes here are structurally sound, streets are well-kept, and tenant quality tends to be higher. Properties typically sell in the $90,000 to $145,000 range, with rents running $800 to $1,100 per month for a 3-bedroom home.
Highlawn

Highlawn sits just south of the Marshall University campus and benefits directly from student and faculty housing demand. This is a prime area for small multi-family deals — duplexes and triplexes that can be purchased for $80,000 to $130,000 and rented unit-by-unit for strong returns. Turnover is higher here, so factor in vacancy and management costs.
Central City

Central City is the higher-risk, higher-reward zone. Properties are cheaper — sometimes $20,000 to $50,000 — but vacancy, blight, and neighborhood instability require an experienced hand. Wholesale deals flow out of this area regularly. Investors who know how to screen tenants and manage distressed properties can build substantial portfolios here at minimal cost basis.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Huntington WV
Wholesale Deals

Huntington's high rate of distressed properties, absentee owners, and probate situations makes it a productive market for wholesalers. Motivated sellers are not hard to find — many inherited properties are sitting vacant, and out-of-state heirs often want to liquidate quickly. A successful wholesale deal in Huntington might involve a property under contract at $35,000 that gets assigned to a cash buyer for $45,000, leaving the wholesaler a $10,000 fee. Learn more about the strategy in our guide to [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners).
Fix and Flip

Flipping in Huntington requires discipline around the numbers because the ARV ceiling is real. A property bought at $45,000 with $35,000 in rehab costs has a total investment of $80,000. If finished comps in that neighborhood max out at $105,000, your gross profit is only $25,000 before carrying costs, closing costs, and profit split. That's still a workable deal, but there's little room for error. Stick to light-to-medium rehabs and focus on cosmetic updates that deliver the highest return per dollar spent: kitchens, bathrooms, paint, and flooring.
Rental Properties and BRRRR Strategy

Huntington may be one of the best small markets in the country for the BRRRR strategy — Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat. Low acquisition costs mean you need less capital to get started, and rental demand from hospital workers, university employees, and local working-class families provides consistent occupancy. A well-executed BRRRR in Huntington can get most or all of your initial capital returned through a cash-out refinance, allowing you to recycle money into the next deal.

The best real estate markets aren't always the flashiest ones. Small Midwestern and Appalachian cities with stable employment anchors and low price points often outperform coastal markets on a cash-flow basis by a wide margin.
Local Market Trends to Watch in 2024 and Beyond

items: Rising rental rates: Average rents in Huntington have increased 8-12% over the past two years as housing supply tightens and construction costs limit new inventory.
Revitalization investment: The city has received state and federal funding for downtown and infrastructure improvements, which could lift surrounding property values over the next 5-10 years.
Healthcare expansion: Cabell Huntington Hospital's ongoing expansion is creating new jobs and driving demand for workforce housing within a 10-minute commute.
Absentee owner inventory: A significant share of Huntington's housing stock is owned by out-of-state landlords or heirs, creating a steady pipeline of motivated sellers.
Low days on market for move-in ready homes: Fully renovated properties in Westmoreland and Enslow Park are moving in under 30 days, confirming buyer demand at the top of the price range.

sections.content: How to Find Off-Market Deals in Huntington WV

The best real estate deals in Huntington WV are rarely listed on the MLS. To access the real inventory, you need to think like a local even if you're investing from across the country. Direct mail to absentee owners and tax-delinquent properties is one of the most reliable strategies in this market. Driving for dollars — or using software to do it virtually — can surface motivated sellers before anyone else has made contact. You can also build relationships with local probate attorneys, property managers, and wholesalers who already have deal flow. For a full breakdown of these approaches, read our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals).
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Huntington WV

items: Build a reliable local team first: Find a property manager, a general contractor, and a real estate attorney in the Huntington area before you close your first deal. This is non-negotiable for remote investing.
Understand the flood zone risk: Parts of Huntington sit near the Ohio River and Fourpole Creek. Always check FEMA flood maps before purchasing and factor flood insurance costs into your underwriting.
Don't skip the inspection: Older housing stock means older systems. Budget for roof, HVAC, plumbing, and electrical updates even on properties that look fine on the surface.
Use conservative vacancy assumptions: Budget for 10-15% vacancy in your cash flow projections, especially for Central City and student-adjacent rentals with higher turnover.
Visit once before scaling: Even one trip to walk neighborhoods and meet your team in person will dramatically improve your decision-making going forward.

Is Huntington WV Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Huntington WV is not a market for investors chasing rapid appreciation or luxury flips. It is, however, an excellent market for investors who prioritize cash flow, low entry costs, and consistent deal volume. The combination of affordable housing, a stable renter population, and a healthy supply of distressed inventory makes it one of the more investor-friendly small cities in the region. If your goal is to build a portfolio that generates monthly income and lets you recycle capital efficiently, this market rewards the disciplined investor who does their homework.
